children: Taiwan reportedly plans to raise billions of dollars to develop industrial parks in the US that would build a base for a comprehensive supply chain for Nvidia Corp.
and other AI hardware makers in the country.
The initiative is starting with a complex in Texas that would cost as much as $4B to build,
Bloomberg
reported, citing Taiwan’s Minister of Economic Affairs Kung Ming-hsin.
The facilities would help smaller suppliers that are essential to the operations of Nvidia’s
main production partner, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
, and AI server assemblers, including Foxconn Technology Group (
) to set up shop in the US, Kung said.
The development comes as Quanta Computer (
) recently received approval to spend $973M to support assembling servers and peripheral equipment in Tennessee. And last month, Wistron
was approved to spend $150M on a U.S. subsidiary that assembles circuit boards. It plans to spend another $146M to renovate a Texas plant.
Taiwan's economy minister in September

Taiwanese companies are planning an additional $20B of investments in the U.S., driven by strong demand for AI applications and semiconductor products. The planned investment is separate from TSMC's (
) U.S. expansion. The world's largest contract chipmaker announced a further $100B investment in Arizona in July, bringing its total planned U.S. investment to $265B.
Nvidia
relies on suppliers including TSMC
, SK hynix
, Samsung Electronics
, and Micron Technology
for chip manufacturing and memory, while its major customers include Microsoft
, Amazon
, and Meta Platforms
. Apple
, meanwhile, is working with suppliers TSMC and Foxconn to support its manufacturing and supply chain operations.

title: Taiwan plans $4B Texas hub for AI, Nvidia suppliers
